Q1.title: Header row not on the first row
Q1.question: Course files often have title lines above the column names. The plan only offers "the first row holds column names: yes or no".
Q1.reading_used_here: Literal: the first row is the header. Each affected fixture also gives the result if the preview let the student pick the header row.

Q2.title: Reserved words as names
Q2.question: A column or table called Order, Group or Select must be quoted in every query, which the naming rule set out to avoid.
Q2.reading_used_here: Literal: the name is kept as it is.

Q3.title: Accented letters in names
Q3.question: Is é one of the "other characters" that become an underscore?
Q3.reading_used_here: Yes: only A to Z, a to z, 0 to 9 and underscore are kept, so Café becomes Caf_.

Q4.title: Underscores at the ends of names
Q4.question: "Amount (£)" becomes Amount_ and "% Change" becomes _Change.

Q5.title: Numbering of blank headers
Q5.question: Is a blank header in the fifth column called column_5 or column_1?
Q5.reading_used_here: By position: column_5. A file with no header row gets column_1 to column_n.

Q6.title: What counts as a plain number
Q6.question: The plan covers leading zeros, currency, separators, percent, decimal commas and exponents. It does not mention +5, .5, 5. or a number with spaces round it, or a decimal column that also holds whole numbers.
Q6.reading_used_here: +5, .5, 5. and " 3" keep the column TEXT, because storing them as numbers would change what was written. Whole numbers and decimals together make a REAL column.

Q7.title: A column with no values
Q7.question: Every row is empty, so the INTEGER rule is met by default.

Q8.title: Blank lines and blank rows
Q8.question: A completely empty line in a CSV, a line of only spaces, a line of only delimiters, and an empty row inside a sheet.
Q8.reading_used_here: An empty CSV line is skipped. A line of spaces is a row whose first field holds those spaces. A line of only delimiters, and an empty row inside a sheet, are rows of NULLs.

Q9.title: Detecting a file with no header row
Q9.question: The plan says the header setting is detected, not how.
Q9.reading_used_here: no_header.csv should be detected as having no header. Treat this as a soft expectation.

Q10.title: Excel number formats
Q10.question: A cell shows £1,234.50, 12.5% or 00123 but holds 1234.5, 0.125 or 123.
Q10.reading_used_here: The stored number is imported, not the displayed text. Only date formats change what is imported. A numeric cell is a number whatever its size.

Q11.title: Excel times and durations
Q11.question: The plan covers dates and dates with times, not a cell holding only a time, or a duration such as 30:00:00.
Q11.reading_used_here: Text as HH:MM:SS, with hours allowed to pass 24 for a duration.

Q12.title: Excel true and false cells
Q12.question: Store 1 and 0, or the words?
Q12.reading_used_here: The words TRUE and FALSE, as Excel shows them.

Q13.title: Formulas with no stored result
Q13.question: Files written by Python libraries hold formulas but no calculated values, so there is no "last calculated value" to import.
Q13.reading_used_here: NULL, and the import report says how many formula cells had no value.

Q14.title: Hidden rows and columns
Q14.question: Filtered-out or hidden rows and columns on a visible sheet.
Q14.reading_used_here: Imported like any other. Hidden and very hidden sheets are listed but not ticked.

Q15.title: Merged cells
Q15.question: A merged block holds its value in the top-left cell only.
Q15.reading_used_here: The top-left cell gets the value and the rest are NULL.

Q16.title: Where a sheet's table starts and ends
Q16.question: Sheets that are empty, hold only formatting, start at C5, have a stray value far from the table, or are chart sheets.
Q16.reading_used_here: The table is the smallest rectangle holding every value. A sheet with no values cannot be imported and is shown unticked and disabled. Chart sheets are not listed.

Q17.title: More than 2,000 columns
Q17.question: SQLite refuses a table with more than 2,000 columns.
Q17.reading_used_here: Refuse the file with a message that says why.

Q18.title: Files that are not what their extension says, or are damaged
Q18.question: A web export saved as .xls is often HTML or tab-separated text. Students also rename files. Some files are cut short or password-protected.
Q18.reading_used_here: Read by content when the content is recognisable; otherwise refuse with a clear message. Never leave a half-made database.

Q19.title: Dates in January and February 1900
Q19.question: Excel counts a 29 February 1900 that never existed (serial 60).
Q19.reading_used_here: Follow Excel: serial 60 is 1900-02-29, serial 59 is 1900-02-28, serial 61 is 1900-03-01.

Q20.title: How numbers are written on export
Q20.question: The plan says plainly, with a decimal point and no rounding. JavaScript prints 1.0 as 1 and 0.0000001 as 1e-7.
Q20.reading_used_here: A REAL always has a decimal point (1.0) and never an exponent (0.0000001). An INTEGER is written in full, including values above 2^53.

Q21.title: What cannot survive export then re-import
Q21.question: An empty string and NULL both export as an empty field. A text column holding only digits re-imports as INTEGER.
Q21.reading_used_here: Accepted. export.json lists the exact differences for each table, so the round-trip check can allow for them.

Q22.title: Exporting a BLOB
Q22.question: The plan does not say.
Q22.reading_used_here: Undecided: there is no expected CSV for mixed_types.

Q23.title: Line ending on export
Q23.question: The plan does not say.
Q23.reading_used_here: CRLF after every record, including the last. Line breaks inside a field are left as stored.

Q24.title: Names of exported files
Q24.question: Table names can hold characters a file name cannot (sales/2024), can collide once cleaned, and can be reserved on Windows (con).
Q24.reading_used_here: The import naming rule is applied to the table name, and duplicates gain _2. con.csv is left as it is.

Q25.title: The Excel export
Q25.question: Added to the plan's decisions table after the fixtures were designed. Sheet names are limited to 31 characters, a cell to 32,767 characters.
Q25.reading_used_here: export.json states what each sheet must hold. There is no binary file to compare against.

Q26.title: Text that starts with = + - or @
Q26.question: Opened in Excel, such a field in a CSV is treated as a formula.
Q26.reading_used_here: Written exactly as stored, as the plan says. The files are meant for Tableau.
